title: Decide what next: iterate, scale or stop
summary: Use what you have learned to decide the product's next step: keep improving it, invest to grow it, or stop and move the team to something more valuable.

beginner: Bring together the results, user feedback and post-launch review.
Ask: did it meet its goal, partly meet it or miss it?
If it met it, look at what would help it grow.
If it partly met it, pick the biggest problem to fix next.
If it missed, consider stopping. Stopping frees the team for better work.
Write the recommendation and agree it with your sponsor.
intermediate: Assess results against the goal and the cost of continuing.
Recommend iterate, scale or stop, with evidence.
Set the next goal and metric if continuing.
experienced: Compare continuing with the best alternative use of the team.
Watch for sunk-cost thinking in yourself and stakeholders.
Plan how to retire features cleanly if stopping, including user communication.
Update the roadmap and strategy to match.

toolExamples.confluence: Record the decision on the product brief page so the history is in one place.
toolExamples.google-docs: Write a short decision memo with evidence for and against.
toolExamples.claude: Paste your results summary and ask it to argue for the option you are not recommending.

pitfalls: Carrying on because of effort already spent
Scaling before the product works well
